note: Per-vendor profile pages under /supply-chain/<slug>. Facts policy: every claim carries a source URL; fields we cannot source are omitted — never invented. Rendering: src/routes/supply-chain/$slug.tsx joins this file's segments ids back to data/vendors.json (the directory layer stays the single source for segment membership). Prerender URL truth derives from the slugs here (vite.config.ts + scripts/check-nav.mjs). Adding a profile = one object here + the company must already have a row in vendors.json.

profiles.name: CoolIT Systems
profiles.tagline: Direct liquid cooling specialist — liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air CDUs, cold plates and rack manifolds; its DLC technology cools the Frontier exascale supercomputer.
profiles.ownership: Subsidiary of Ecolab (acquisition closed July 2026, ~$4.75B); previously majority-owned by KKR with Mubadala alongside (2023-2026)

productLines.name: CHx2000 CDU
productLines.note: Row-based liquid-to-liquid CDU: 2,000 kW at 5 °C approach, 2,125 LPM; supports up to 12 NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks, group control of up to 20 CDUs

productLines.name: AHx240 / AHx180 CDUs
productLines.note: Self-contained liquid-to-air CDUs that reject heat to room air, for sites without facility water

productLines.name: OMNI all-metal cold plates
productLines.note: All-metal unibody cold plates (no O-rings/gaskets) for NVIDIA, Intel and AMD CPUs/GPUs; unveiled May 2024, shipping at scale from June 2024

productLines.name: Rack manifolds & TCS piping
productLines.note: Modular piping, valves and rack manifolds distributing coolant from CDUs to server racks

facts.text: Ecolab closed its ~$4.75B acquisition of CoolIT (announced March 2026, closed July 2026), folding it into Ecolab's AI cooling platform
Launched the CHx2000 row-based CDU: 2 MW capacity in a 750×1200 mm footprint, supporting up to twelve NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks
Unveiled the OMNI all-metal unibody cold plate architecture for NVIDIA/Intel/AMD processors
CoolIT DLC technology supports Frontier, the first US exascale supercomputer at ORNL (fully fanless, liquid-cooled)

profiles.ocp: Contributor to the OCP Cooling Environments cold plate sub-project — listed on the Single-Phase Direct-to-Chip Cold Plate Test Specification V1.0.0.

faq.q: Who owns CoolIT Systems?
faq.a: Ecolab — the acquisition closed in July 2026 for ~$4.75B. Before that CoolIT was majority-owned by KKR (2023-2026) with Mubadala investing alongside.

faq.q: How big is the CoolIT CHx2000 CDU?
faq.a: 2,000 kW at 5 °C approach temperature with 2,125 LPM flow; one unit supports up to 12 NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks, and up to 20 CDUs can run in group control.

profiles.name: Asetek
profiles.tagline: Danish pioneer of warm-water direct-to-chip server cooling — integrated pump-and-cold-plate D2C coolers plus the InRackCDU (up to 80 kW/rack); its data center hardware line is now listed as heritage technology after the 2021 HPC exit.
profiles.ownership: Acquired by CQXA Holdings Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) via 2026 takeover offer — 90% passed April 14, 2026, compulsory acquisition initiated, Oslo Børs delisting to follow; previously Oslo Børs: ASETEK

productLines.name: D2C ingredient coolers
productLines.note: Integrated pump-and-cold-plate assemblies for direct-to-chip cooling inside servers — low-profile drop-in replacements for air heat sinks that fit 1U chassis (listed under heritage technology)

productLines.name: InRackCDU
productLines.note: 4U rack-level warm-water liquid-to-liquid CDU: up to 80 kW of heat per rack, rejecting to facility water as warm as 45 °C for chiller-free operation (listed as legacy)

productLines.name: RackCDU D2C system
productLines.note: Warm-water server-level direct-to-chip system; independent NREL testing (2014) evaluated its energy performance — Asetek claimed >50% cooling energy savings and free cooling in most climates

facts.text: CQXA Holdings (Singapore) takeover passed 90% of shares (final result April 14, 2026), triggering compulsory acquisition and planned Oslo Børs delisting
Exited the HPC niche segment of its data center business to refocus on other segments
Announced ongoing collaboration with Intel on hot-water liquid cooling for servers and data centers

faq.q: Does Asetek still sell data center liquid cooling?
faq.a: Its data center hardware (D2C ingredient coolers, InRackCDU) is listed on asetek.com under heritage/legacy technology after the company exited the HPC segment in 2021. Verify current availability before specifying.

faq.q: Who owns Asetek?
faq.a: CQXA Holdings Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) — its 2026 takeover offer passed 90% of shares on April 14, 2026, initiating compulsory acquisition and a planned Oslo Børs delisting.

profiles.name: Boyd Corporation
profiles.tagline: Thermal-management veteran — 5M+ liquid cold plates delivered to hyperscalers, rack manifolds and megawatt-class CDUs; its thermal business is now part of Eaton.
profiles.hq: Boca Raton, Florida, USA (current official site; pre-divestiture sources list Modesto, CA)
profiles.ownership: Boyd Thermal (liquid cooling) sold to Eaton for $9.5B — announced Nov 2025, completed March 2026; the remaining Boyd (Engineered Materials) stays with Goldman Sachs Alternatives (since 2019)

productLines.name: ROL2300 CDU
productLines.note: High-capacity in-row liquid-to-liquid CDU: up to 2.3 MW at 8 °C approach (1.15 MW at 4 °C); one unit cools 10+ NVIDIA NVL72 racks; custom Alfa Laval brazed-plate heat exchanger

productLines.name: Liquid cold plates
productLines.note: Direct-to-chip cold plates for AI processors — 5 million delivered to hyperscalers as of Sept 2025

productLines.name: CDU portfolio, rack manifolds & cold plate loops
productLines.note: CDU range including 4U in-rack models, plus rack manifolds and loops for end-to-end direct liquid cooling

facts.text: Eaton completed its $9.5B acquisition of Boyd Thermal (announced Nov 2025, completed March 12, 2026); Boyd's Engineered Materials business continues independently under Goldman Sachs Alternatives
Announced 5 million liquid cold plates delivered to hyperscalers through high-volume global manufacturing
Launched the ROL2300 CDU with 2.3 MW capacity for AI liquid cooling
Showcased Google's 2 MW Project Deschutes CDU (an OCP-ecosystem design) that Boyd manufactures, at the 2025 OCP Global Summit

profiles.ocp: Exhibits at the OCP Global Summit; manufactures Google's OCP-ecosystem Project Deschutes 2 MW CDU. Formal corporate membership not verifiable from public sources.

faq.q: Is Boyd still independent?
faq.a: Its liquid-cooling business is not: Eaton completed the $9.5B acquisition of Boyd Thermal in March 2026. The remaining Boyd Corporation (Engineered Materials) continues independently under Goldman Sachs Alternatives.

faq.q: What is Boyd's largest CDU?
faq.a: The ROL2300 in-row liquid-to-liquid CDU: up to 2.3 MW at 8 °C approach (1.15 MW at 4 °C), cooling 10+ NVIDIA NVL72 racks per unit.

profiles.name: Motivair
profiles.tagline: Data center liquid cooling specialist (now 'Motivair by Schneider Electric') — CDUs up to 3.5 MW, dynamic cold plates, ChilledDoor rear-door heat exchangers and chillers; its CDUs cool six of the world's top ten supercomputers.
profiles.ownership: 75% controlling stake acquired by Schneider Electric for ~$850M (announced Oct 2024, closed February 2025); remaining 25% expected to be acquired by 2028

productLines.name: CDU line (MCDU / WCDU)
productLines.note: Liquid-to-liquid CDUs scaling from 105 kW to 2.5 MW (MCDU-70, Jan 2026); the WCDU (Sept 2026) reaches 3.5 MW at 1.5 L/min per kW with up to 20 units combinable; certified for NVIDIA hardware

productLines.name: ChilledDoor rack cooling system
productLines.note: Active rear-door heat exchanger removing up to 75 kW per rack with 100% heat removal

productLines.name: Dynamic cold plates
productLines.note: Direct-to-chip cold plates for 100 kW+ AI racks; listed support includes AMD SP3/SP5, AMD Instinct MI300A/MI300X, Intel Ice Lake and Sapphire Rapids, NVIDIA SXM5

productLines.name: Heat Dissipation Unit (HDU) & chillers
productLines.note: Liquid-to-air HDU with 100 kW of heat rejection for liquid-ready racks without facility water; free-cooling/air-cooled chillers and TCS loops

facts.text: Launched the WCDU — up to 3.5 MW at 1.5 L/min per kW, integrating liquid and air cooling for flexible deployments
Schneider completed the acquisition (February 2025); Motivair now operates as 'Motivair by Schneider Electric'
Schneider Electric agreed to acquire a 75% controlling interest in Motivair for ~$850M cash

profiles.ocp: OCP Global Summit participant (2024 showcase; listed as 'Motivair by SE' in the 2026 participating-companies list).

faq.q: What is Motivair's relationship to Schneider Electric?
faq.a: Schneider Electric acquired a 75% controlling stake for ~$850M (announced October 2024, closed February 2025) and expects to acquire the remaining 25% by 2028. Motivair operates as 'Motivair by Schneider Electric'.

faq.q: What capacity range do Motivair CDUs cover?
faq.a: Liquid-to-liquid CDUs from 105 kW (MCDU-70 line, up to 2.5 MW as of Jan 2026) to the WCDU at 3.5 MW (Sept 2026, 1.5 L/min per kW, up to 20 units combinable).

profiles.name: Vertiv
profiles.tagline: Critical-infrastructure vendor whose CoolChip CDU line (70 kW to 2,300 kW, liquid-to-air and liquid-to-liquid) distributes coolant for direct-to-chip and rear-door cooling in AI data centers.

productLines.name: CoolChip CDU family
productLines.note: 70-2,300 kW across liquid-to-air (CDU 70) and liquid-to-liquid (CDU 121/600/1350/2300) in-rack/in-row form factors; next generation of the Liebert XDU line

productLines.name: CoolChip CDU 2300
productLines.note: In-row liquid-to-liquid CDU: 2,300 kW at 4 °C approach, positioned as the most compact footprint in its class for hyperscale AI

productLines.name: CoolChip CDU 70
productLines.note: In-row liquid-to-air CDU: 70 kW at 11 °C approach — adds direct-to-chip cooling where no facility water exists

productLines.name: MegaMod CoolChip
productLines.note: Prefabricated turnkey AI infrastructure with integrated CoolChip liquid cooling, cited in the NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 blueprint

facts.text: Co-developed with NVIDIA a 7 MW power-and-cooling reference architecture for GB200 NVL72 — 132 kW per rack with hybrid liquid-air cooling using XDU CDUs
Announced two new high-capacity CDUs at SC24: CoolChip CDU 2300 kW (liquid-to-liquid) and CoolChip CDU 350 kW (liquid-to-air)
Relocated its US corporate headquarters to Westerville, Ohio

profiles.ocp: Active OCP member — has served on OCP committees and co-authored papers; ships OCP-validated racks, power shelves and the CoolChip CDU 121, and built CoolChip CDUs to Google's Project Deschutes (5th-gen OCP) spec at up to 2 MW.

faq.q: What capacity range does the Vertiv CoolChip CDU line cover?
faq.a: 70 kW to 2,300 kW: liquid-to-air CDU 70 (70 kW at 11 °C approach) for sites without facility water, and liquid-to-liquid CDU 121/600/1350/2300 in in-rack and in-row form factors (CDU 2300: 2,300 kW at 4 °C approach).

faq.q: How is Vertiv involved with NVIDIA GB200 NVL72?
faq.a: It co-developed a 7 MW power-and-cooling reference architecture with NVIDIA for the GB200 NVL72 platform — 132 kW per rack with hybrid liquid-air cooling — and its MegaMod CoolChip prefabricated module is cited in the NVIDIA blueprint.

profiles.name: Delta Electronics
profiles.tagline: Power and thermal management supplier offering chip-to-system liquid cooling for AI data centers — GoCool liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air CDUs, cold plates and two-phase immersion.

productLines.name: GoCool liquid-to-liquid CDUs
productLines.note: Facility-water CDU family: GoCool-660, 1000, 1200, 1500 and 3000 — 660 kW to 3,000 kW

productLines.name: GoCool liquid-to-air CDUs
productLines.note: In-row CDUs rejecting heat to air: GoCool-80, 150 and 260 — 80-260 kW

productLines.name: In-rack CDU
productLines.note: Rack-level CDU managing up to 250 kW with modular rack manifold, shown at SC25

productLines.name: Liquid cooling plates
productLines.note: GPU/CPU cold plates including a 6,200 W liquid cooling plate and a Micro Channel Lid with 20% more heat-exchange area; two-phase immersion also listed (no published kW rating)

facts.text: GoCool 3 MW liquid-to-liquid CDU now shipping for next-generation AI data centers
At SC25 showcased a 2 MW in-row CDU (500 GPM) supporting Google's Project Deschutes open architecture (±400 VDC, 5th-gen OCP spec), alongside the 250 kW in-rack CDU and chip-to-system cold plates

profiles.ocp: Its 2 MW in-row CDU is designed to Google's Project Deschutes open architecture per the 5th-generation OCP spec (±400 VDC).

faq.q: What is Delta's GoCool CDU range?
faq.a: Liquid-to-liquid: GoCool-660 through GoCool-3000 (660 kW to 3 MW, the 3 MW unit shipping since 2026). Liquid-to-air: GoCool-80/150/260 (80-260 kW). Plus a 250 kW in-rack CDU shown at SC25.

faq.q: How does Delta relate to Google's Project Deschutes?
faq.a: Delta showcased a 2 MW in-row CDU (500 GPM) built to Project Deschutes — Google's open cooling architecture following the 5th-generation OCP spec with ±400 VDC power.

profiles.name: Stäubli
profiles.tagline: Swiss quick-disconnect specialist whose OCP-compliant UQD/UQDB dry-break couplings are a de-facto standard interface for direct-to-chip liquid cooling in AI data centers.

productLines.name: UQD universal quick disconnect
productLines.note: DN 6 mm manual rack-to-hose coupling, max 16 bar, stainless steel — OCP-compliant, NVIDIA RVL-approved (published L/min figures: not published)

productLines.name: UQDB blind-mate
productLines.note: Blind-mate coupling DN 3/6/7/10 mm, max 16 bar, 0.8 mm misalignment tolerance, for blade servers and dense racks

productLines.name: TDN 2-inch high-flow couplings
productLines.note: Large-bore symmetrical transfer couplings for rack/CDU-level coolant feed, aimed at AI racks up to 785 kW

productLines.name: Mini-QD
productLines.note: Micro quick disconnect enabling direct liquid cooling of OSFP/QSFP optical pluggables (introduced with Ciena)

facts.text: UQD and UQDB connectors approved by NVIDIA and added to its Recommended Vendor List for next-generation GPUs
At the OCP Global Summit: unveiled Mini-QD (Ciena liquid-cooled OSFP enabler) and announced the UQD v2 spec with tighter flow-performance limits and standardized geometry
The OCP Universal Quick Disconnect spec was created by a working group including Stäubli, Parker and CPC

profiles.ocp: Co-author of the OCP UQD specification (2020, with Parker and CPC); driving UQD v2 and Mini-QD standardization; UQD listed on the OCP Marketplace.

faq.q: Did Stäubli help write the OCP UQD standard?
faq.a: Yes — the OCP Universal Quick Disconnect spec was created in 2020 by a working group including Stäubli, Parker and CPC; Stäubli is now driving the UQD v2 spec with tighter flow-performance limits and standardized geometry.

faq.q: Are Stäubli UQD couplings NVIDIA-approved?
faq.a: Yes — UQD and UQDB connectors were approved by NVIDIA and added to its Recommended Vendor List for next-generation GPUs (2025).

profiles.name: CPC (Colder Products)
profiles.tagline: Quick-disconnect specialist whose Everis UQD couplings (developed with Intel to the OCP spec) provide the dripless rack- and cold-plate-level connections used in hyperscale AI liquid cooling.
profiles.ownership: Dover Corporation (NYSE: DOV) — business unit of PSG within Dover

productLines.name: Everis UQD02 / UQD04
productLines.note: Latched OCP UQDs in 1/8-inch and 1/4-inch flow paths, 303 stainless steel, thumb latch and redundant multi-lobed seals (per-series L/min figures: not published)

productLines.name: Everis UQD06
productLines.note: UQD series with a 3/8-inch flow path added for higher-flow AI liquid cooling (2025)

productLines.name: Everis UQDB04 and UQD08/UQDB08
productLines.note: Blind-mate OCP UQDs: UQDB04 in 3/8-1/2-inch terminations; UQD08/UQDB08 hybrid set in 5/8-3/4-inch stainless steel

productLines.name: Everis BLQ / LQ series
productLines.note: Purpose-built liquid cooling QDs (latched, blind-mate, metal and high-performance plastic) beyond the UQD standard

facts.text: Launched the Everis UQD06 series, adding a 3/8-inch flow path to the UQD family for AI's higher-flow needs
The OCP Universal Quick Disconnect spec was created by a working group including CPC (with Stäubli and Parker); CPC developed its Everis UQDs with Intel to the spec

profiles.ocp: Member of the original 2020 UQD spec working group; Everis UQD developed in collaboration with Intel per the OCP specification.

faq.q: What UQD sizes does CPC offer?
faq.a: The Everis family spans UQD02 (1/8-inch) and UQD04 (1/4-inch), the 2025-added UQD06 (3/8-inch) for higher AI flows, and blind-mate UQDB04 plus UQD08/UQDB08 (5/8-3/4-inch) — all to the OCP UQD standard.

faq.q: Who owns CPC?
faq.a: CPC (Colder Products Company) is a business unit of PSG within Dover Corporation (NYSE: DOV).

profiles.name: LiquidStack
profiles.tagline: Immersion cooling pioneer — two-phase and single-phase DataTanks plus direct-to-chip CDUs for AI-scale heat loads.
profiles.ownership: Trane Technologies announced its acquisition on 2026-02-10 (following a 2023 minority investment); expected to close in early 2026, closing not yet confirmed

productLines.name: DataTank (two-phase immersion)
productLines.note: Flagship two-phase immersion tanks in 2U/4U/8U/48U sizes; ran Wiwynn OAI servers at partial PUE 1.02-1.03 with zero water for heat rejection

productLines.name: Single-phase immersion DataTank
productLines.note: Launched Nov 2023: >110 kW per full-size tank at ASHRAE W3 water, >2.8 kW/U, fits the footprint of four 19"/21" racks, supports OCP and ORv3 form factors

productLines.name: CDU 1.X / CDU 2.X (direct-to-chip)
productLines.note: Coolant distribution units for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, including a CDU-1MW class; rapid-deployment and high-flow variants for high-density AI racks

productLines.name: GigaModular CDU
productLines.note: Scalable centralized CDU for large AI deployments; described by LiquidStack as supporting NVIDIA Vera Rubin platforms

facts.text: Trane Technologies announced it will acquire LiquidStack (Feb 10, 2026), placing it in Trane's Commercial HVAC Americas business; CEO Joe Capes continues to lead. Closing expected early 2026, not yet confirmed
Unveiled its first single-phase immersion offering: >110 kW per tank at ASHRAE W3 conditions (>2.8 kW/U)
Debuted the world's first immersion-optimized OCP Open Accelerator Infrastructure (OAI) servers at SC21 — Wiwynn OAI servers with Habana Gaudi processors in a LiquidStack DataTank

profiles.ocp: OCP-adjacent firsts: debuted the first immersion-optimized OAI servers at SC21 (2021); two-phase immersion promoted at the 2021 OCP Global Summit (Microsoft deployment).

faq.q: Does LiquidStack do direct-to-chip as well as immersion?
faq.a: Yes. Beyond its two-phase and single-phase DataTank immersion lines, LiquidStack sells direct-to-chip coolant distribution units (CDU 1.X / 2.X including a CDU-1MW class, and the GigaModular CDU described as supporting NVIDIA Vera Rubin platforms).

faq.q: Who owns LiquidStack?
faq.a: Trane Technologies announced on 2026-02-10 that it will acquire LiquidStack, after a 2023 minority investment; the deal was expected to close in early 2026 and no closing announcement had been published when this profile was last reviewed. Verify current ownership before contracting.

profiles.name: Baltimore Aircoil (BAC)
profiles.tagline: Heat rejection for liquid-cooled data centers — cooling towers, hybrid and dry coolers — plus the COBALT single-phase immersion system.
profiles.ownership: Wholly owned subsidiary of Amsted Industries (since 1985)

productLines.name: TrilliumSeries Dry Cooler
productLines.note: Water-free axial-fan dry cooler for water-stressed sites; up to 10,000 MBH (~2.9 MW) per unit, vertical coils, independent fans/VFDs/coils for redundancy

productLines.name: FXV3 Closed Circuit Cooling Tower
productLines.note: Combined-flow closed-circuit tower positioned by BAC for data centers; capacity not published on the product page

productLines.name: HXV Hybrid Cooler
productLines.note: Hybrid wet/dry cooler — BAC cites up to 70% water savings vs traditional fluid coolers and up to 60% more energy efficiency than air-cooled systems

productLines.name: COBALT Immersion Cooling System
productLines.note: Pairs a CorTex single-phase immersion tank (16/32/38/48RU, 19" and 21" servers, PUE up to 1.05 claimed) with BAC outdoor heat rejection

facts.text: BAC's CorTex immersion tank certified under the Intel Data Center Certified Solution for Immersion Cooling program for 4th/5th-gen Xeon — program developed with Intel, ExxonMobil, Hypertec and Micron (Dec 2, 2025)
Launched upgraded CorTex-powered immersion tanks (Oct 9, 2025) in 16/32/38/48RU sizes as the indoor half of the COBALT system
Houston colocation deployment: COBALT single-phase immersion with BAC heat rejection ran year-round without mechanical cooling

profiles.ocp: Listed in the OCP membership directory; no project-level contributions verifiable from public sources.

faq.q: What does BAC make for liquid-cooled data centers?
faq.a: The heat-rejection half of the loop: TrilliumSeries water-free dry coolers (up to 10,000 MBH ≈ 2.9 MW per unit), FXV3 closed-circuit towers, and HXV hybrid coolers (BAC cites up to 70% water savings) — plus the COBALT single-phase immersion system that pairs a CorTex tank with BAC outdoor heat rejection.

faq.q: Are BAC immersion tanks certified?
faq.a: Yes — the CorTex tank was certified (Dec 2025) under the Intel Data Center Certified Solution for Immersion Cooling program for 4th/5th-gen Xeon, a program developed with Intel, ExxonMobil, Hypertec and Micron.
